newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down in quiet trading.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower after players stayed sidelined despite returning to the market after a long year-end break, traders said.
They said there were some inquiries for nearby SMR grades, but could not report any business.
"They (buyers) either have enough rubber or are not prepared for any short-covering yet," said a trader.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted February RSS1 buyer at 314 cents ($1.25) a kg, down two cents from Friday. February SMR20 was priced a cent lower at 309.50 cents a kg.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 307 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 367, SMR L at 347, SMR 5 at 317, SMR 10 at 309 and drum latex FOB at 239.

Traders said on last Friday that prices could dip further this week if fresh demand was not seen. Sunny skies since the start of January has created an ample supply of latex and other materials, which was pressuring prices downwards, they said.
The INRO five-day average was 241.91 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 3 from 241.81 on Jan 2. The daily indicator was 242.09 against 242.16 previously.
